newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition tells Congress to withdraw claim.
newsitem.headline: India coalition tells Congress to withdraw claim.

text.p: India's defeated United Front coalition on Thursday told the Congress to withdraw its official claim to form a government before an agreement could be reached on the election of a new alliance leader.

"The letter is proving to be a stumbling block," a senior United Front official told reporters, referring to Congress president Sitaram Kesri's claim to President Shankar Dayal Sharma on March 31, seeking to head a new government.

The official's comment followed several meetings between United Front Convener Chandrababu Naidu and Kesri to end the political uncertainty triggered by the fall of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government in a vote of confidence on April 11.
"There are problems which need to be sorted out," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters earlier on Thursday. "I am confident that all problems will be resolved."
Reddy said the 15-party coalition's decision-making Steering Committee would meet at 9.30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Friday to elect a new leader to replace Deve Gowda.
The Press Trust of India said Kesri held informal consultations with the decision-making Congress Working Committee on Thursday to resolve the political impasse.
